messages.text:
Hi,

I'm considering trying the HarloOS firmware on my BS-4.

A few questions...  Is the HarloOS supported under warranty?  And is it possible to get the original OEM firmware in case Harlo isn't working well?  I tried it on a Naja Duo and it seemed to get hot way too fast at normal (non-overclock) voltage and frequency.

Thank you,
Scott
Searched the web · Harlo OS Bitfortun BS-4 firmware
Searched the web · harlolabs.com Harlo OS supported models download
Handed to the team · No BS-4 stock firmware image in our docs (Bitfortun has not published BS-4 sourc

Hi Scott,

Thanks for asking before you flash. That's the right order to do it in.

Harlo OS does support your unit. The Bitfortun BS4 is on the current supported list on our Harlo OS page, next to the Naja Duo you already tried. Harlo OS is our own firmware, made by Harlo Labs and given away free by us. It isn't a third party image.

On the warranty: one rule I can state firmly is that overclocking voids it, whatever firmware you run. Overclocking means running the unit above the hashrate it's sold at, which for the BS-4 is 18 TH/s. If you try Harlo OS, keep it at stock frequency and voltage. If you've changed them, the stock values are one click away in the dashboard. I don't want to guess at the rest of the warranty answer, so I've asked JD, our hardware lead and the developer of Harlo OS, to confirm in writing that a BS-4 on Harlo OS at stock settings stays covered.

On getting the original firmware back: I don't have a Bitfortun BS-4 image I can point you to, and I can't confirm a way to go back yet. Bitfortun has published source code for the BS-1 but not for the BS-4. JD will confirm whether there's a stock BS-4 image and how to restore it. If going back matters to you, I'd wait for his answer before flashing. One more thing if you do flash: the "factory" install option wipes your settings and the "OTA" option keeps them. Either way, write down your pool URL, worker name and your current frequency and voltage first.

On the Naja Duo running hot: that's useful feedback, and I've passed it to JD as well. If you go ahead with the BS-4, flash the latest BS4 build listed at https://harlolabs.com/ rather than an older download. Then watch the temperatures for the first half hour at stock settings, and if it runs hotter than it did on the original firmware, go back to stock values. It would help JD a lot to know which Harlo OS version the Naja Duo was on and what temperatures you saw.

JD picks this up tomorrow at 10am ET, and his answer will come to you by email. If you'd like it sooner, the Harlo OS channel on our Discord is very active and JD answers there himself: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf (mention @nullhashrate).

Best,
Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support
